title: Towel product review
summary: NH reviews the humble towel as a training tool: what kind to pick and how he uses it for plate grip holds, towel curls and towel pull-ups. Towels free up the wrist, train finger strength and can help lifters reach deeper scapular retraction on pull-ups.
claims: Pick a short, slightly rough towel (a dish towel works); too long is cumbersome and too soft is slippery
Towel exercises are low-load, and most towels can handle 200+ lb, far more than you'll use
NH moved from bands (damaged) to chains (hurt his hands) to towels for his plate grip exercise
Plate grip: thread the towel through a plate hole, grab both ends and squeeze; plates with holes near the edge allow a short towel and many stacked plates
Like rings, towels let you change wrist angle without discomfort, so towel curls hit muscles at angles a dumbbell can't
Towel pull-ups are harder to grip than a bar but differ from fat grips: they hurt the fingers and build finger and forearm strength, useful for climbers
Towel pull-ups free the wrist, elbow and shoulder, allowing deeper scapular retraction while keeping tension on the upper back
If you struggle with full ROM for lat hypertrophy, start with towel pull-ups and carry the range over to regular pull-ups
Washing towels makes them smoother and less grippy; they get better the more you use them
exercises: towel through plate hole, wrap hand, squeeze
